D.t: Everett Wess trails by 12.8 and wins 3% of simulations. Closing it takes about 109,560 voters switching sides, or 219,121 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +20.9 and R +4.7. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +11.1. Your best recent poll is Chism Strategies (D) at R +9.4; your worst is The Alabama Poll at R +21.2. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 80,800 votes; Montgomery, a projected net 31,994 votes; Madison, a projected net 9,789 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Madison, D +6.7, 8.5% of the vote; Mobile, D +2.1, 7.8% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, D +3.7, 3.9% of the vote; Lee, R +11.7, 3.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Everett Wess runs furthest behind in Coffee, Cullman, Baldwin. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 67% of voters, 43 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 42 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.17 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 48 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.94 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Everett Wess: Immigration voters 15 to 84, White voters 33 to 66, Small counties 36 to 63. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$18K cash against $627K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Everett Wess. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $16.8M helping Barry Moore and $0 helping Everett Wess.

R.t: Barry Moore leads by 12.8 in the forecast and wins 97% of simulations. The cushion is about 219,121 votes; a one point swing is about 8,580 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +4.7 and R +20.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +11.1. Your best recent poll is The Alabama Poll at R +21.2; your worst is Chism Strategies (D) at R +9.4. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Baldwin, a projected net 44,796 votes; Cullman, a projected net 24,131 votes; Shelby, a projected net 18,467 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Madison, D +6.7, 8.5% of the vote; Mobile, D +2.1, 7.8% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, D +3.7, 3.9% of the vote; Lee, R +11.7, 3.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Barry Moore runs furthest behind in Talladega, Jefferson, Tuscaloosa. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 67% of voters, 56 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 57 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.17 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 51 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.94 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Barry Moore: Black voters 20 to 80, Independents 24 to 74, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 34 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$627K cash against $18K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Barry Moore. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
